summary: Hardened /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 to ignore execution, setuid, and device nodes via persistent fstab entries (tmpfs with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime), verified functionally before and after a full node restart with a confirmed boot_id change.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline mount state: /dev/shm was tmpfs with nosuid,nodev but exec allowed; /tmp was not a separate mount (part of root ext4), and no systemd tmp.mount unit existed.

Backed up /etc/fstab, removed any pre-existing /tmp or /dev/shm entries, and appended hardened entries: 'tmpfs /tmp tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0' and 'tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0'.
Applied changes live: mounted /tmp from the new fstab entry and remounted /dev/shm with the new options.
Verified via findmnt that both /tmp and /dev/shm show nosuid,nodev,noexec.
Functionally proved noexec by creating and chmod +x'ing a script in each location and confirming execution was denied ('Permission denied').
Created a setuid-bit file (mode 4755) in each location to demonstrate the setuid bit is set but mount carries nosuid (execution itself already blocked by noexec, confirming defense-in-depth).
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime on node1.
Issued a native, single-node, non-destructive reboot via 'sudo -n reboot' backgrounded so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect.
Polled node1 until exec access returned.
Confirmed boot_id changed (f9bf293d... -> 11f47d59...) proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce.

Re-verified post-reboot that /tmp and /dev/shm still show nosuid,nodev,noexec (proving fstab persistence) and re-ran the exec-block functional test successfully, plus basic read/write sanity checks on both mounts.

evidence.requirement: Baseline state before changes (mounts, fstab, OS)
evidence.summary: Showed /dev/shm as tmpfs (nosuid,nodev, exec allowed) and /tmp as part of root ext4 with no separate mount or systemd tmp.mount unit, establishing the pre-change state on Ubuntu 24.04.

evidence.requirement: /tmp and /dev/shm mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev and change applied/persisted via fstab
evidence.summary: Batch script added fstab entries, mounted /tmp and remounted /dev/shm, and findmnt confirmed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime on both.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that execution and setuid are ignored on both mounts
evidence.summary: Chmod +x scripts on /tmp and /dev/shm failed to execute (Permission denied); setuid-bit copies were created showing nosuid mount semantics apply.

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline boot identity captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3 and confirmed hardened mounts/fstab entries present prior to reboot.
Issued 'sudo -n reboot' backgrounded on node1; stream closed as expected when the node went down, indicating the reboot command was accepted.

evidence.requirement: Node polled until command execution available again
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node still rebooting); second poll succeeded, confirming node1 came back online.

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just uptime/service change)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id 11f47d59-24db-4419-a45e-b2191ca53b34 differs from pre-reboot boot_id f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required mount hardening and data functionality
evidence.summary: After reboot, findmnt still shows nosuid,nodev,noexec on /tmp and /dev/shm (fstab persistence confirmed), exec-block functional test passed again, and basic write/read sanity checks succeeded on both mounts.
